recipes.name: Willard Family German Chocolate Cake
ingredients_raw: 1 (4 ounce) package sweet baking chocolate (such as Baker's German's Sweet Chocolate®) - broken into pieces

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour three 8-inch cake pans and line bottoms with parchment paper.
To make the chocolate cake: Stir chocolate into boiling water until melted; set aside to cool.
Beat 1 cup of softened butter with 2 cups of sugar in a large bowl with an electric mixer until lighter in color and fluffy. Stir in 4 egg yolks, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Beat in 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract and cooled chocolate mixture until thoroughly blended.
Sift flour, baking soda, and salt into a bowl; mix into chocolate cake batter, alternating with buttermilk, in 3 or 4 additions. Beat until batter is smooth, about 1 minute.
Beat egg whites in a metal or glass bowl until stiff peaks form when the beaters are lifted straight up; gently fold into chocolate cake batter, keeping as much volume as possible.
Pour batter into prepared cake pans.

Bake in the preheated oven until the cakes have browned lightly and a toothpick inserted into the center of a cake comes out clean, 35 to 40 minutes. Cool cakes in pans for 10 minutes before turning out onto wire racks to cool completely.

To make the pecan coconut frosting: Pour evaporated milk into a large saucepan. Mix in 1 cup of sugar, 3 egg yolks, 1/4 cup of butter, and 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to medium, and cook until thickened, stirring constantly, about 12 minutes.
Remove from heat and mix in coconut and pecans, beating until frosting has cooled and is spreadable.
Spread frosting between each layer and on top of the cake. Enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Willard Family German Chocolate Cake
raw_recipe.description: This moist German chocolate cake is made from scratch with luscious layers of chocolate cake and coconut pecan frosting for a family favorite!

review.reviewBody: Fabulous! This was my first attempt at a German Chocolate cake, I kind of expected it to be a little more complicated but this was easy. I had to use the milk and vinegar substitute for the buttermilk because I forgot to bring my list to the store and of course forgot the buttermilk :( It worked fine. I used butter in both the cake and the frosting since I never have margarine. I also made some chocolate frosting for the sides of the cake, I didn't have enough of the coconut frosting but I think that is because I'm a little heavy handed with frosting. My family was sad when this cake was gone and there was a fight over the last piece ( I won! ) Thanks for the great recipe, its a keeper.

**Edited based on making this again as cupcakes :)...Everyone raved about this cake - I've never made it before and I think it came out great. I wanted my frosting to cover it entirely, so ended up with little bare spots around the edges that I filled in with chocolate frosting ("Creamy Chocolate Frosting" by Tracy on this website). The frosting is only meant to cover the top and in between layers so make more if you want it to be more rich and/or have more full coverage....I've since made this again as cupcakes! I've posted a picture of them. I followed the recipe to a 't'. Did not make any modifications and again received RAVE reviews! People went out of their way to tell me how great they were....To make them into cupcakes I filled the paper cake cups to about 2/3-3/4 full, and baked at 350 for about 18 minutes. You know they are ready when the tops look porous like sponges and the edges get just a little bit brown. Also, use a toothpick :) I was able to make 24 cupcakes out of this recipe, and the coconut frosting was the perfect amount for them. I used my same chocolate frosting to fill in around the edges.

Great cake. Made it for my husband on our anniversary. I substituted some of the boiling water with some coffee. I would strain the frosting mixture over a colander in case you accidentally cook some of the egg (like I did).

I didn't have buttermilk, so used the dairy I had (3/4 C sour cream, 1/4 c cream with a little vinegar). I used two 10-inch pans instead of the three 8-inch, and baked on 325°F (I find the lower temp bakes with less dome and more moist) I made 1 1/2 batch of frosting using the full 12 Oz can of milk, 1 cup white sugar, 1/2 cup brown sugar, teaspoon vanilla, 1/2 teaspoon rum flavor, toasted pecans, and the coconut I used half unsweetened, half sweetened. Best German chocolate cake I've had in my life.

Love this recipe! My mom's birthday is on Christmas Day. To make the day special for her, Dad always had her favorite, German Chocolate cake, for dessert with Christmas dinner. He continued that tradition after she passed on in 2016, and when he passed on in 2021, I went looking for a recipe so I could continue to remember Mom's birthday. I tried almost a dozen recipes, and this one won the prize with the family. It is easy, quick, and delicious! We don't like a lot of frosting, so one recipe of the frosting is enough for me to cover the cake with a thin layer. We also have a nut allergy, so I leave out the nuts. I don't own 8-inch cake pans, so I use 2-9-inch cake pans instead. I have to extend the baking time to 45 minutes. Enjoying this cake is a beautiful reminder of my mom's birthday. Thank you for sharing your family recipe and helping me remember my mom!

I made this recipe three times. My brother said the first time the cake was an eight and the icing was a 10. By the third time, it was moist, and perfect. Thank you, it's wonderful as is. One hint: I added coffee instead of water to the chocolate mix. I used butter instead of margarine. Also, I iced the cake when it was still a little warm, then stuck it in the fridge. It went to a party, and it was a hit. My Aunt said it was better then my grandma's, and trust me, my grandma is cursing me in heaven right now because she was the best cook on the face of the earth.
Doubled the icing. A must to let the cakes and icing cool completely so it doesn’t slide off the cake.

Cake came out great. I don't know if it was me, but it could use a little more sugar. Also greasing the pans are a necessity because I lost a layer due to under greasing. Another tip to cool off the frosting is to refrigerate it so its easier to spread! Third time making this and will continue to do so!!

The recipe looks complex but is so worth it! I'm not a very experienced baker so was a bit worried but followed the instructions to the letter and it came out perfect :)

Just a note: the picture contains butter icing not in the recipe on the sides. Budget a bit of exra marge, icing sugar and cocoa for that :)

Oh my! This is one delicious cake. We made this for Easter dinner and decided to do it a little differently. We used the topping between layers and on top of the cake. Then we frosted the sides with chocolate butter cream frosting. We topped it off with malted milk Easter eggs. It looked like a little next. We will use this recipe again and again.

Aug, 2023 This was hard to make! Haven’t tasted it yet. I doubled the frosting and barely had enough. This was my first attempt ! I only make biscuits lol but they are very good! As another review noted, the chocolate was melted with water. It would be better done with butter. But great recipe even if it was difficult for a beginner. Dec 29,2023 I have now made this 3 times. The main change has been melting the chocolate in butter rather than water. Makes it richer. Everyone loves it! Now it’s requested for family gatherings.
I want to go to the Willard Family Reunion if this is how you all cook! A moist and delicious cake and icing.
Made this exactly as written. Turned out great! Though I think I would double the frosting next time.
It was delicicious! First time was a little daunting but am remaking it today and doubling the icing!
First time making German Chocolate cake and it turned out great!
The cake is very moist and delicious.

Excellent!! It was very simple. I followed the recipe exactly, but I used two 7 inch pans (because I like tall cake layers). I also made a chocolate frosting for the sides and to pipe a border around the coconut/pecan frosting. I served it for guests, and they LOVED IT! One of the guests said it tastes exactly like his mother's German chocolate cake from his childhood. Definitely my go-to recipe for German chocolate cake from now on.

I have been making German Chocolate Cakes for years. Up until now, I have always used the recipe I found on the package of German Chocolate. Then I discovered this recipe which was basically the same except that it included more of most ingredients. For example there are four eggs instead of three, 2 1/2 cups of all-purpose flour instead of 3/4 cups of cake flour, more butter and more sugar. I make this cake every year for my sister's birthday so decided to give this recipe a try this year. It did not disappoint! I found it easier to make and it was nice and moist...much more so than the other recipe. I made it in two 9-inch round pans...I was going to do the three layers with 8 -inch pans but was afraid it wouldn't fit in my cake carrier as I had to take it out to another family member's house. Since I only made two layers, and only wanted frosting on the top and between the two layers, I used the frosting recipe from my original recipe which called for lesser amounts of ingredients. It worked well. From now on, this will be my "go to"recipe for German Chocolate Cake. Next time, I would like to try the 3 layers! Thanks for sharing this recipe!
I’ve used this recipe a few times and it’s definitely one of my favorite cake recipes! I have to force myself to share it!
Great recipe easy to follow The only problem was finding the German chocolate bars
